result:
Perfect! I've successfully implemented the comments feature with community moderation. Here's what was delivered:

## Implementation Summary

### Database & Models
- Added `comments` table with post_id, user_id, body, and created_at fields
- Added `comment_reports` table with unique constraint on (comment_id, user_id) pairs
- Created `Comment` and `CommentReport` models with proper relationships
- Updated `Post` model to include `hasMany` relationship with comments
- Set up cascade delete so posts automatically remove their comments

### API Endpoints
- `POST /posts/:id/comments` - Create a comment (1-2000 characters, authenticated only)
- `DELETE /comments/:id` - Delete comment (comment author or post author only, returns 303 redirect)
- `POST /comments/:id/report` - Report a comment (idempotent, always returns 204)

### Frontend
- Updated the posts/Show page to display comments (sorted oldest first)
- Shows comment author name and creation timestamp
- Comment form for signed-in users
- Delete button for comment authors and post authors
- Report button for all signed-in users (shows "Reported" after reporting)
- Comments with 3+ reports are hidden from the page but preserved in the database

### Authorization & Validation
- Guests are blocked from commenting/reporting/deleting by authentication middleware
- Only comment authors or the post author can delete a comment
- Comment body is validated: required, 1-2000 characters
- Reporting is idempotent: reporting twice by the same user counts as one report
- Re-reporting returns 204 with no additional data

### Testing
- 19 new tests covering all functionality: store, destroy, report, cascade delete, and rendering
- All tests pass with proper isolation and cleanup
- Tests verify authorization, validation, idempotency, and comment visibility rules

All CI gates (codegen, typecheck, lint, check, audit, test) are passing.
